newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania mediator to focus on "imperilled" election.
newsitem.headline: Albania mediator to focus on "imperilled" election.

text.p: International mediator Franz Vranitzky has cancelled a trip to rebel-held southern Albania and turned his attention to question marks hanging over the elections promised in June.

President Sali Berisha and his party -- who accepted the formation of an all-party government last month to curb Albania's headlong plunge into anarchy -- have started laying down stiff conditions for going ahead with the planned vote.
An Italian-led multinational security force which arrived this week is now guarding the main port of Durres and has been checking roads and bridges to ensure the safety of aid convoys.

Vranitzky decided after meeting the president on Wednesday not to travel to Vlore, a hotbed of anti-Berisha feeling, or to the northern town of Skhoder as planned on Thursday, his spokeswoman Melissa Fleming said.

The former Austrian chancellor, now an envoy of the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe, wanted to focus his two-day trip to Albania "on the situation here and on preparing for elections," she said.

She said Vranitzky would visit the south on a later trip. Vranitzky has urged the government -- which includes both Berisha's supporters and his opponents -- and rebel leaders to start talks to pave the wave for elections by June.
But Berisha said on Wednesday rebel committees controlling much of southern Albania were hindering progress towards the vote and must be disbanded.
Rebels seized control of the south earlier this year as they blamed Berisha for the savings frauds which cost many Albanians their savings.
Nearly 300 people were killed in unchecked violence after people looted arsenals deserted by police and troops.
Vranitzky said the deadlock over how to deal with the rebels meant that the elections were "in a way imperilled".
Albania's Justice Minister said it would be impossible to disarm the population in time for the planned election in June.
Spartak Ngjela told a meeting with Vranitzky that the government should nevertheless make it an offence to possess weapons during the voting period in an effort to ensure calm.
"The population is almost entirely armed today. It is impossible to disarm the population... in two months," he said. "A partial disarmament... will not be sufficient for the elections".
Heavily armed French troops guarded emergency supplies of flour and beans at the port of Durres on Wednesday after they were unloaded from a relief ship for delivery to isolated areas of Albania.
Troops from the multinational security force that arrived in Albania on Tuesday may begin escorting the World Food Programme's first big shipment within days, workers from the U.N. food agency said.

French armoured personnel carriers sped from the dismal port of Durres on the Adriatic to the capital Tirana, past armed police checkpoints, testing the road and bridges before convoys of humanitarian aid fan out across Albania.

"We're examining the bridges to make sure there's no chance they'll collapse when heavy aid convoys cross over," said a French army captain at the port where small groups of heavily armed infantrymen patrolled.
